Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for carving out the time, um i'm Samir from Redwood AE. quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: hi i'm maya, head of mops at boreal orbit. we're looking to put a summarization + agent feature into our mission ops dashboard.
[00:20] Jonas: jonas, cto. here to make sure infra and security line up with our compliance program.
[00:26] Ravi: ravi - platform lead, i'll be doing the integration work.
[00:30] Tara: tara from security and compliance. i'll own SOC2 and key mgmt questions.
[00:36] Lena: lena - customer success at redwood. i'll run the onboarding and ops playbook.
[00:40] Diego: diego - solutions engineer, i'll handle benchmarks and runtime mapping.

[00:48] Samir: cool, quick agenda: align on pilot use case, confirm deployment mode, agree on success metrics, and set owners for the pilot. sound right?
[00:56] Maya: yes. we want a two-week pilot, low risk, integrate into our dashboard for internal ops users only.

[01:10] Ravi: couple constraints, we have strict egress rules and everything goes through our VPC, we prefer private deployment but we'd like to explore hosted first if security can be satisfied.
[01:25] Samir: yeah that's common — we support hosted, dedicated, and private VPC. for initial proofs some customers start hosted with VPC peering / private endpoints, others go straight private. there are tradeoffs: hosted is fastest to start, private gives you full control.

[01:41] Tara: our checklist: SOC2 attestation, KMS/HSM integration for key material, SSO with SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC that maps to our groups, and audit logs forwardable to our SIEM. also data residency guidance would be good.
[01:59] Lena: we can share our security pack and a SOC2 summary; we also have a VPC onboarding diagram for private installs.

[02:10] Diego: from a technical perspective, for the pilot we usually recommend a small model variant — quantized — to validate latency and correctness. we can run a benchmark harness with your prompts and measure p50/p95 latency, throughput at target concurrency, and cost-per-token estimates.
[02:29] Ravi: we plan to send 75–150 simultaneous users hitting the dashboard, each query ~400 tokens typical, some longer threads. latency p95 target 300–400ms for short summarization inference, longer for multi-turn.

[02:45] Samir: ok that's great to scope. Diego, we'll need to set up continuous batching / kv caching config tuned for that pattern — prefix caching for repeated threads helps a lot.
[02:56] Diego: noted. i'll propose batching windows and cache TTLs once i see token distributions.

[03:08] Maya: timeline: we want pilot in two weeks and then decision by month end to expand. is that feasible?
[03:16] Samir: aggressive but doable if we get infra access and SAML metadata quickly.

[03:25] Tara: question — for private deployment, do you support our HSM via bring-your-own-kms or do we need to use your managed keys?
[03:34] Lena: both options exist. for Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM via standard key wrapping; we'll share details in the security pack.

[03:43] Tara: also audit log format — we need indepth event logs for every inference request including token counts and model version.
[03:51] Diego: audit logs included; we can forward to a S3 or direct to your SIEM via secure forwarder. slight caveat: in hosted mode logs are redacted by default for PII, but we can enable token-level telemetry under an enterprise agreement.

[04:05] Jonas: cost — rough numbers? we ran a quick spike on aws with a small gpus and it got expensive.
[04:13] Samir: we will share a cost model — Redwood Optimize suggestions like quantization, batching, and caching can reduce unit cost significantly. for the pilot we can estimate cost-per-call and show tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated.

[04:28] Ravi: connectivity — is there a way to use private endpoints + mutual TLS?
[04:34] Diego: yes, we can do private endpoints with mTLS, also VPC peering or private link depending on cloud provider. we'll include network playbook.

[04:46] Maya: who from your side will own the playbook and runbook?
[04:50] Lena: me — i'll be primary, Samir will own commercial items, Diego will handle SE tasks. we'll provide a 10-step runbook for staging → pilot → production.

[05:02] Samir: ok quick demo plan for the next meeting — diego will spin up a small staging cluster, run the harness, and we'll review results. is 10th of march ok for the benchmark review?
[05:11] Ravi: yes that works.

[05:18] Tara: on compliance, we may require a short security deep dive before any production keys are exchanged.
[05:23] Lena: understood — we'll schedule that with our security engineering lead.

[05:30] Diego: technical note: for multi-turn state we maintain kv cache; if you run on private you can pin model versions and we can enable deterministic rollout policies. slight mis-speech there: i mean model pinning for canary and rollback.

[05:48] Maya: about data retention — we do not want any customer data persisted outside our tenancy.
[05:54] Samir: for private deployment data does not leave your VPC. for hosted we offer zero-retention options for enterprise customers — we'll outline the guarantee.

[06:05] Jonah: (interruption) sorry jonas — question re: latency SLOs, do you commit?
[06:09] Samir: we offer SLO-backed SLAs on Dedicated plans. hosted has best-effort SLOs with transparent performance metrics. Dedicated + private options give more predictable p95.

[06:22] Ravi: okay let's talk specifics: access — do you need an IAM role or a service account?
[06:27] Diego: for VPC/private we need a cross-account role for provisioning and optionally a bastion for troubleshooting. for hosted we just need IP allowlist or private link + service principal.

[06:40] Tara: do you have SOC2 audit docs we can share with procurement?
[06:44] Lena: yes, i'll upload the SOC2 summary and our security pack to the shared drive after the call.

[06:50] Samir: commercial — pilot pricing: we can do a short-term pilot credit + limited support. i'll put together the SOW options.

[07:00] Maya: okay great. a couple of to-dos on our end: we'll provide SAML metadata, KMS policies, and example prompt set.

[07:07] Ravi: plus network contact for peering.

[07:10] Samir: perfect. Diego, any technical blockers you foresee?
[07:14] Diego: nothing major. i'll need auth details and a sample dataset to tune caching and batch windows. also need a couple of representative prompts to reproduce session patterns.

[07:25] Maya: note — we do a lot of streaming replies in the UI so streaming support is important.
[07:30] Diego: we support streaming in both hosted and private runtimes; minor differences in buffer tuning.

[07:38] Tara: legal — can we get a copy of your data processing addendum?
[07:42] Samir: yep i'll attach the DPA and the pilot terms with the email.

[07:48] Jonas: i'd like to see the runbook and an ops playbook for incident response.
[07:52] Lena: that's part of the runbook package we'll send. includes incident flows and contact list.

[07:59] Samir: ok let's recap next steps briefly.
[08:03] Samir: action items: samir send pricing and pilot SOW; lena share runbook + security pack; diego spin up staging harness; tara provide SOC checklist + KMS notes; ravi provide network contact and SAML metadata.
[08:20] Maya: schedule security deep dive for next week please.
[08:24] Lena: scheduling poll after call.

[08:30] Ravi: minor nit, will you provide a mockup of the telemetry dashboard?
[08:34] Diego: yes, we'll share sample dashboards and a quickstart notebook.

[08:40] Jonas: ok thanks everyone, excited to get started.
[08:43] Maya: thanks.
[08:45] Samir: thanks team — we'll follow up with materials.
